questions.q: What is the programme mainly about?
options: Whether we can reduce harm from disasters
A park ranger who survived being hit by lightning
How climate change is causing more earthquakes
Why disasters are reported so often in the news
questions.why: Neil asks if anything can be done to stop natural disasters, or if they are beyond our control.

questions.q: Why do the presenters say Roy Sullivan was lucky or unlucky?
options: He lost his job as a park ranger
He was hit by lightning seven times and survived
He lived through a huge earthquake
He escaped a hurricane with his family
questions.why: Roy was struck by lightning on seven different occasions and survived them all.

questions.q: Why do the presenters expect things to get worse in the future?
options: Because countries are spending less on safety
Because there are more earthquakes each year
Because of climate change and growing populations
Because people ignore warnings
questions.why: Neil says things will get worse due to climate change and increasing populations.

questions.q: Why does Professor Lucy Easthope dislike the phrase 'natural disaster'?
options: It is too difficult for the public to understand
It blames people for the disaster
It is a new phrase that nobody uses
It suggests nothing can be done, so people give up
questions.why: She says 'natural' implies fatalism and a sense of 'let's give up now'.

questions.q: What does Beth say about the 'additional harm' after a disaster?
options: It is often worse than the disaster itself
It is impossible to prevent
It only affects roads and buildings
It happens only in poor countries
questions.why: She says this additional harm, like disease or destroyed buildings, is often worse than the disaster.

questions.q: Why does Neil say an earthquake in the ocean is 'less of a disaster'?
options: Because ocean earthquakes are always smaller
Because computers can stop them
Because fewer people live there than in a city
Because they never cause tsunamis
questions.why: He compares it with an earthquake in a populated city, where more people are at risk.

questions.q: What has happened in Bangladesh since its new warning system started?
options: Cyclones have become less frequent
Deaths from cyclones have fallen a hundred times
People have moved away from danger zones
The system has been replaced by computers
questions.why: Beth says Bangladesh has seen a hundred-fold decrease in cyclone deaths.

questions.q: According to Professor Ilan Kelman, what is the most important thing for people in the danger zones?
options: Having bicycles so they can escape quickly
Buying their own megaphones to warn others
Receiving money from the government
Being able to return to their homes and jobs
questions.why: He says most importantly they can return afterwards to their homes and their livelihoods.
